question: An engineer implements an environment with multiple traffic types on a consolidated I/O link between Cisco Nexus 9000 Series Switch and MDS 9000 Series Switch. The configuration must meet these requirements: the unified I/O link must support LAN and SAN traffic; a single, multipurpose Ethernet transport must be used; the configuration must discard MAC addresses that are not part of the current fabric; and the QoS markings must be preserved. Which configuration set meets the requirements?
options:
MDS-A(config)# interface fcip4 -
MDS-A(config-if)# use-profile 8 -
MDS-A(config-if)# peer-info ipaddr 200.200.100.7

N9K-2(config)# interface Eth2 -
N9K-2(config-if)# switchport mode trunk
N9K-2(config-if)# auto qos trust dscp

MDS-B(config)# interface fc3 -
MDS-B(config-if)# switchport trunk mode on
MDS-B(config-if)# switchport trunk allowed vsan 2-5

N9K-1(config)# fcoe fcmap 0e.fc.1d
N9K-1(config)# int vfc 1 -
N9K-1(config-if)# bind interface e1/3
theory: A single, multipurpose converged Ethernet link between a Nexus and MDS switch that must carry both LAN and SAN traffic, discard MAC addresses foreign to the fabric, and preserve QoS markings is exactly what FCoE provides: configuring a distinct 'fcoe fcmap', so only FPMAs belonging to this fabric are accepted and any others are discarded, and creating and binding a vfc interface to the physical Ethernet interface is the FCoE-specific configuration needed - FCIP (a WAN/IP-based FC tunneling technology) and plain FC trunking don't provide a single unified Ethernet transport for both LAN and SAN traffic. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 9 - FCoE Addressing / FC-MAP)
